final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful but not sufficient to move the outcome to compliant_with_caveats. A caveated-compliance finding would require admissible evidence that the remaining compliance predicate was actually satisfied, such as exclusion of the affected use case, approved risk acceptance, or completed required disclosure where policy permits launch on that basis. The current record still shows the enterprise refund workflow segment is below target, remains exposed in the cohort, the available risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not address that exposure, and no completed pre-launch disclosure is in evidence. The narrowed position supports an operational-readiness characterization, but it does not resolve the live policy-compliance gap.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the affected enterprise refund workflow is excluded from the rollout cohort.
No approved risk-acceptance record addresses the exposed enterprise refund workflow segment.
No admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch disclosure was actually completed for the named launch use case.
The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate the weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance exists; that predicate remains unmet.
Operational launch-readiness evidence remains stronger than the evidence for policy-compliant certification.
